title: Logo marquee
sub: Endless logo rows with soft edge fades

KestrelMeridianCobaltFathomOrbitalQuillKestrelMeridianCobaltFathomOrbitalQuill
prompt: Build an endless logo marquee for a "Trusted by" section. Render one row of logos twice back to back inside a flex track with width: max-content, give every logo a right margin (not gap, so the half-width math stays exact), and animate the track with @keyframes { to { transform: translateX(-50%) } } at 20s linear infinite so the loop is seamless. Add a second row moving the other way (animation-direction: reverse, 26s) for depth. Fade both edges with mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, #000 16%, #000 84%, transparent) on the row wrapper. Use monochrome logos at a muted color so no single brand shouts. Animate transform only. Pause on hover (animation-play-state: paused), mark the duplicate set aria-hidden="true", and keep a static visually hidden list of the company names for screen readers. Put the real text in the DOM for screen readers, never rely on color alone, and under prefers-reduced-motion show the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

Add a one-line caption below with the real number. Use real avatars with alt="" in production and give the group a single aria-label such as "Joined by 2,400 makers". title: Star rating
sub: Stars fill one by one to 4.9
prompt: Build a star-rating block that fills to 4.9. Draw five star SVGs (24 viewBox, rounded joins). Each star is two stacked copies: a pale outline copy as the base and an accent-filled copy on top that is clipped with clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0), revealed to inset(0 0 0 0) over about 400ms with cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1), staggered 190ms per star. The fifth star stops at inset(0 10% 0 0) so 4.9 reads as nearly full (compute the percent as (1 - fraction) * 100 for any rating). Pop each star as it fills with a brief scale(1.25) and a slight-overshoot spring. Tick the big score from 0.0 to 4.9 in sync using requestAnimationFrame and toFixed(1) with tabular-nums. Trigger on scroll-in. Give the group role="img" and aria-label="Rated 4.9 out of 5 from 3,120 reviews". Put the real text in the DOM for screen readers, never rely on color alone, and under prefers-reduced-motion show the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

Show a small "Live" pill with a dot that pulses (a ::after copy of the dot scaling from 1 to 3.2 while fading out, 1.6s ease-out infinite), a large tabular-nums number (about 46px, tight tracking) and a caption "people signed up this week". Every second or so add one to three to the number: swap the text and play a short entrance on the digits (translateY(40%) with opacity .2 to rest in 460ms with cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1)) inside an overflow: hidden wrapper, and pop a green "+2 just now" chip that fades in with a slight-overshoot spring and leaves after 800ms. Optionally add a tiny 7-bar week chart whose last bar grows with scaleY as the count rises. Drive real numbers from your backend over SSE or polling, throttle updates so the page never flickers, and announce changes sparingly with aria-live="off" plus a periodic polite summary. title: Award badge
sub: A rosette badge with a shine and tilt
prompt: Build an award badge with a shine sweep and a subtle tilt. Draw the badge as an inline SVG (viewBox 0 0 100 100): a scalloped rosette polygon with 36 alternating points at radius 48 and 43, filled with your accent gradient, an inner thin white ring, a white star, and two text lines ("TOP RATED" in small caps with letter-spacing, and the year in bold). Define the same polygon as a clipPath and place a skewed rect filled with a horizontal white gradient (transparent, 70% white, transparent) inside a group that uses that clipPath, then animate the rect's transform from translateX(0) skewX(-18deg) to translateX(230px) skewX(-18deg) every 3.6 seconds with cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1) so the glint only shows on the badge. Wrap the SVG in a perspective container and sway it between rotateY(-16deg) and rotateY(16deg) over 6s ease-in-out, with a soft drop-shadow. Add a caption below naming the award. Give the SVG role="img" and an aria-label. Put the real text in the DOM for screen readers, never rely on color alone, and under prefers-reduced-motion show the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

Keep every fact visible at all times in the DOM (the highlight only emphasizes), so nothing important is hidden by the animation. title: Review score ring
sub: A tick ring lights up to 4.8 of 5
prompt: Build a review score ring made of tick marks. Draw an inline SVG (viewBox 0 0 120 120) with 50 short round-capped lines placed around a circle, from radius 46 to 55, starting at 12 o'clock (angle = i / 50 * 2PI - PI/2). Unlit ticks use a pale tint; light the first 48 (4.8 / 5 = 96%) in your accent color in order over about 1.8 seconds with an ease-out-cubic curve driven from requestAnimationFrame, giving the leading tick a lighter accent so the fill head reads. Put the score in the middle (36px semibold, tabular-nums, "out of 5" beneath) and tick it from 0.0 to 4.8 in sync, with a row of five small filled stars and the review count ticking up to 2,318 underneath. Trigger once on scroll-in. Give the ring role="img" and aria-label="Rated 4.8 out of 5 from 2,318 reviews". This is a score display, not a loading spinner. Put the real text in the DOM for screen readers, never rely on color alone, and under prefers-reduced-motion show the final state with no movement. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.
